findings.title: The `arch` (pre-slice-plan) boundary cannot find its artifact or reach the review-gate branch
findings.description:
- **Wrong index.** `detectDocuments` matches `${idx}-review.${reviewType}.` against the index it is given (`documentDetector.ts:66-96`). An arch review is named for the initiative, e.g. `240-review.arch.*.md`. The design says the data flow is identical for `arch` (line 168), using the slice `index`. That index is the active slice (241) and would look for `241-review.arch.*`. The design never says the `arch` gate must use `extractSliceIndex(project.fileArch)`.
- **No slice index in this state.** `deriveSliceStatus` returns `{name:'', index:null, status:'no-active-slice'}` at `WorkflowNavigator.ts:453-455` when `fileSlice` is unset, so it has no index to give.
- **Routing never reaches the gate.**
  - `getNext` handles `no-active-slice` in a GUARD that returns on every path (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:98-166`), before the reserved `review-gate` slot at line 248.
  - `detectFirstRunContext` (FR-3b, line 413) already returns "Architecture document exists. Advance to Phase 3" for the arch-exists, no-plan state. The gate has to sit before that call.
  - The design says "evaluated at the points in the cascade where they occur" (line 35) but names no insertion point.
- **No defined status shape.** If `deriveSliceStatus` returned `pending-review` with an empty name and null index, the active-slice path would run instead: arch-file-missing guard, warnings and `buildSummary`. The design does not say what the `SliceStatus` looks like here.
- **Ambiguity when a slice is active.** The design does not say whether the arch gate applies when a slice is active but `status.slicePlan` is null. `parseSlicePlanSafe` also returns null when `totalSlices === 0`.
- **Walkthrough gap.** The Verification Walkthrough (lines 325-374) never exercises the `arch` boundary.

findings.title: Config access is described as synchronous raw values, but `ConfigManager.get` is async, returns `ConfigResult`, and can throw
findings.description:
- **Wrong return shape.** The design says "navigator calls `this.config?.get(...)` and hands raw values to `reviewGate`" (line 109) and that config values are `string | boolean | number` (line 275). `ConfigManager.get` is `async get(key): Promise<ConfigResult>` and the value is in `.value` (`ConfigManager.ts:7-11, 91`).
- **Contradicts itself on ownership.** Line 109 says the navigator resolves config. TD-1 (lines 178, 191) says `resolveGateConfig(config)` in `reviewGate.ts` reads `ConfigManager`. That module is also called "pure".
- **Throws are unhandled and get swallowed.**
  - `get` throws on an unknown key, and on malformed TOML via `readToml`, which rethrows anything that is not ENOENT.
  - `deriveSliceStatus` wraps its body in `catch { return base }` (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:497-499`), so a config throw would silently turn the slice into `no-active-slice`.
  - Slice-plan guidance would then replace the real status, and the gate would fail silently, which the arch's "must not silently pass" and fail-fast principles (240-arch:40, 48) rule out.
- **Gating-off is not byte-identical for a bad config file.** Every surface now always constructs a `ConfigManager` (line 49), so `review_enabled` is read on every call. A malformed `.context-forge.toml` therefore changes `cf next` for users who never enabled gating, contradicting lines 32 and 108.
- **Invalid values are unhandled.** `get` does no enum validation (only `set` does). A hand-edited `review_threshold = "strict"` has no defined handling in `resolveGateConfig`.
- **Per-call cost.** There is no per-call caching. Each `get` reads up to two TOML files, and the design needs about four gets per evaluation.

The design should name who reads and awaits config, what happens on a read failure or invalid value, and how that failure is kept out of the `catch { return base }` path.

findings.title: Review file paths from `detectDocuments` are project-relative, but the data flow passes them straight to `parseFrontmatter`
findings.description:
- **The bug.** `detectDocuments` returns paths joined from `project-documents/user/...` with no `projectPath` (`documentDetector.ts:91-96`). The existing navigator code does `join(projectPath, p)` before reading (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:479`).
- **Why it matters.** The design's `parseFrontmatter(path).data.verdict` omits the join. `parseFrontmatter` never throws, so a relative path resolved against the CWD reads nothing and returns `found:false`.
- **Result.** Every present review would normalize to `UNKNOWN`, and a valid `PASS` would show as `review-failed` under the default `unknownAs=fail`.
- **Cause of the miss.** The "never throws" property the design praises (line 79) is what would hide this.
- **Fix.** State the join explicitly, and add a test with a real fixture and a `PASS` verdict, not only stubs.

findings.title: The `tasks` (pre-implementation) gate has no defined trigger and would block slices already mid-implementation
findings.description:
- **Signal is too broad.** The design says the signal is "task file exists, not complete" (line 138), or "not implemented" (line 25). In the code that is every `in-implementation` state, including 5 of 8 tasks checked (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:496`).
- **Effect on live work.** With gating on and no `tasks` review, a half-finished slice flips from "Continue implementation" to `pending-review`.
- **Effect on newly enabled gating.** Enabling gating on an existing project retroactively blocks work already past that boundary. The design does not say whether the gate should fire only at zero checked tasks, or whether a started slice implies the review is moot.
- **Second `needs-tasks` origin.** `needs-tasks` also arises when a task file exists but parses to zero tasks, or fails to parse (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:482-484`). The design does not say which gate applies there.
- **Gate overlap.** Gates evaluated at different statuses can both be owed (line 57). The design does not give the precedence, for example when `complete` with a missing `tasks` review hits the `code` gate.
- **Tests.** The Technical Requirements (lines 314-315) do not cover any of these cases.

findings.title: New status and recommendation carry no review type, verdict or threshold, and "stable vocabulary" contradicts prose strings
findings.description:
- **Rationale cannot be built from the status.** TD-7 requires the rationale to name the review type, and for `review-failed` also the verdict and threshold. `getNext` only sees `SliceStatus`, via `getStatus` (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:94`). The design adds no fields to `SliceStatus` (`types.ts:255-264`). Line 218 says `reviewGate` "exposes" the verdict and threshold, but nothing carries them across `getStatus` to the `review-gate` branch. Either the branch re-evaluates (duplicating the gate) or `SliceStatus` must grow additively.
- **Runners cannot route on type.**
  - The arch goal (240-arch:32) is that runners act "without parsing recommendation strings".
  - `workflow_status` consumers cannot tell which review is pending.
  - `workflow_next` consumers receive only prose.
- **"Stable" vocabulary vs prose.**
  - The arch specifies `recommendation: "review"` and `"blocked"` (240-arch:118, 124).
  - TD-7 uses prose ("Review required before advancing", "Blocked: review verdict…") with "exact strings finalized in implementation".
  - Line 286 calls these "the stable strings runners route on". They cannot be both stable and left undefined.
  - The sample `pending-review` text hard-codes "code review" and "before advancing", which is wrong for the `slice`, `tasks` and `arch` boundaries.
- **Stale status lists.** `workflow_status`'s tool description lists the four old statuses (`workflowTools.ts:127-129`). The design does not list updating it, and 243 only covers README docs.

findings.title: The `STATUS` const conflates two vocabularies and cannot satisfy the design's own "no magic strings" rule
findings.description:
- **Two vocabularies.** `STATUS` is derived for `NormalizedStatus` (`complete`, `in-progress`, `not-started`, `deprecated`). `SliceStatus.status` is a separate lifecycle union (`types.ts:258`). The data flow (lines 150, 164) uses `STATUS.Complete` as a `SliceStatus.status` value, which only works because the strings coincide.
- **New values not covered.** `pending-review`, `review-failed`, `needs-tasks` and similar are not in `STATUS`. Line 394, "never a bare `'code'` or `'complete'`", cannot be met for them.
- **Mixed style.** Inside `deriveSliceStatus`, new `STATUS.Complete` sits beside the untouched literal at `WorkflowNavigator.ts:492` until 910 lands.
- **Count claim is off.** The "~50 sites" figure (lines 37, 239) does not match the code. A grep of `packages/*/src` finds 65 occurrences of the four literals across 9 files. That count includes non-`NormalizedStatus` uses, so it is not exactly comparable.
- **Fix.** Either define a second const for slice-lifecycle statuses, or say explicitly why one const serves both.

findings.title: Per-gate config mapping is unspecified, and the shipped key descriptions still advertise inert behavior
findings.description:
- **No boundary-to-key mapping.** The design's `Boundary` values are camelCase (`preSlicePlan`, line 185). The keys shipped in 240 are `pre_slice_plan`, `pre_tasks`, `pre_implementation` and `pre_advance` (`ConfigKeys.ts:55-106`). The arch example uses kebab-case (240-arch:82). The mapping is not stated, and an unmapped key would be silently ignored.
- **Misleading descriptions.**
  - The four `review_type` key descriptions say "empty = use the global default; gate logic added in slice 241" (`ConfigKeys.ts:59, 72, 85, 98`). That implies the keys are consumed.
  - The design makes them inert, but excludes touching the descriptions (line 64) and defers explaining them to 243.
  - A user can set a `review_type` today and nothing happens, which clashes with the arch's fail-fast principle (240-arch:48).
- **Unresolved decision.** TD-4 leaves "remove vs. keep inert" as "flagged for the PM at implementation" (line 228). The slice plan (240-slices:28) assigns that call to this design.

findings.title: The design restates content already in the slice plan and elsewhere in itself
findings.description:
The mechanism is right-sized, but the document is heavier than it needs to be. Cuts:
- The Overview boundary table and "Four units of work" repeat the slice plan entry (240-slices:19) and Technical Scope.
- The "Boundary → signal" paragraph (line 141) is repeated nearly word for word in TD-5.
- The "Provides to Other Slices" list restates Technical Scope.
- `positionToReviewType(boundary): string` is a one-line wrapper over `BOUNDARY_REVIEW_TYPE`, and it returns `string`, losing the `as const` literal types. Exporting the const (typed) is enough.
- The "Rejected alternatives" paragraph (line 112) can shrink to one sentence.

findings.title: Existing tests and call sites look compatible
findings.description:
- **Call sites.** The four production call sites named in the design are the only `new WorkflowNavigator()` calls in `src`. Optional constructor injection keeps the existing core tests valid.
- **CLI/MCP tests.** The CLI and MCP tests already mock both `WorkflowNavigator` and `ConfigManager`.
- **Worktree path.** `resolveProject` overlays `projectPath` with the worktree path (`worktree-overlay.ts:9`), so the "worktree scope for free" claim holds for `next` and `status`.
- **Baseline test.** The "240 baseline test" is a single in-implementation assertion (`WorkflowNavigator.test.ts:192`), not a complete set. The gating-off regression should run both with `config` undefined and with an injected stub returning `review_enabled=false`, since the second path is new.
- **Divergence from the arch.** The arch allows an `UNKNOWN` verdict to map to `pending-review` (240-arch:106). This design always maps it to `review-failed`. That is defensible given the `review_unknown_as` enum, but it should be stated as a deliberate deviation.
